title: Union Minister Smt. Annpurna Devi Urges Citizens to Report Child Marriage on Child Helpline 1098 and Realise Resolve of Child Marriage Free Bharat
body_text:
Union Minister of Women and Child Development, Smt. Annpurna Devi has urged citizens not to stay silent if they come across or suspect a child marriage anywhere, and to report it immediately by calling the Child Helpline 1098.
In a post on ‘X’ the Union Minister said that child marriage is not merely a social evil, but a serious blow to the rights, education, health and future of children.
She called upon everyone to come together to protect the dreams, rights and safe future of our daughters, and to make the resolve of a Child Marriage Free Bharat a reality.
बाल विवाह केवल एक सामाजिक कुरीति नहीं, बल्कि बच्चों के अधिकारों, शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य और भविष्य पर गंभीर आघात है। यदि आपको कहीं भी बाल विवाह की जानकारी मिले या इसकी आशंका हो, तो चुप न रहें। तुरंत 1098 पर कॉल कर इसकी सूचना दें। आइए, हम सभी मिलकर बेटियों के सपनों, अधिकारों और… pic.twitter.com/1ciZ4H2wGn — Annpurna Devi (@Annapurna4BJP) August 25, 2026

enrichment.summary: Union Minister for Women and Child Development Smt. Annpurna Devi, via a social media post, urged citizens to report suspected child marriages by calling Child Helpline 1098. She emphasised that child marriage severely harms children's rights, education, health and future, and called for collective action to achieve a 'Child Marriage Free Bharat'.
enrichment.context:
Child marriage remains illegal in India under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, which sets the minimum marriage age at 18 for women and 21 for men, though enforcement gaps persist especially in rural and economically weaker regions. The Child Helpline 1098 is a government-run 24x7 emergency response service for children in distress, including cases of abuse, trafficking, and child marriage, operating under the broader child protection framework alongside the Integrated Child Protection Scheme (ICPS) and POCSO Act. Government surveys such as NFHS-5 have shown a declining but still significant prevalence of child marriage in parts of India, making it a persistent social and public health concern tied to girls' education, health outcomes, and gender equality goals under India's SDG commitments.

This release is a public awareness appeal via social media rather than a new policy announcement, scheme launch, or data release, and does not introduce any new mechanism, funding, or legal change.
